title: Building a Neural Network Engine from First Principles in NumPy
subtitle: How to compute every gradient by hand, understand backpropagation, and achieve 97% accuracy on MNIST without PyTorch.
excerpt: The rule was simple: no autograd, no PyTorch — write matrix backpropagation from mathematical definitions upward.
content: When embarking on deep learning, it is easy to default to frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow where calling `loss.backward()` abstracts away the underlying linear algebra and calculus. I set out to construct a modular feedforward neural network engine using only raw **NumPy**, deriving and checking every gradient by hand.
### Motivation & First Principles

Most machine learning courses introduce backpropagation as a high-level computational graph. But to truly understand why training succeeds or diverges, one must derive the partial derivatives of the loss function $L$ with respect to each weight matrix $W^{[l]}$ and bias vector $b^{[l]}$ across layers $l = 1, \dots, L$.
### Mathematical Derivation of Backpropagation
Consider a dense layer performing linear transformation followed by an activation function $\sigma(Z)$:
Using the multivariate chain rule, the gradient of the loss $L$ with respect to the pre-activation $Z^{[l]}$ is given by:
$$dZ^{[l]} = dA^{[l]} \odot \sigma'(Z^{[l]})$$
where $\odot$ represents the Hadamard (element-wise) product. The gradients with respect to parameters across a batch of $m$ samples are:
### Implementation in Pure NumPy
Translating these equations directly into Python required careful attention to matrix dimensions. Here is the core implementation of the `DenseLayer` class:

```python
import numpy as np

class DenseLayer:
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim):
        # He Initialization for ReLU activations
        self.W = np.random.randn(output_dim, input_dim) * np.sqrt(2.0 / input_dim)
        self.b = np.zeros((output_dim, 1))
        
    def forward(self, A_prev):
        self.A_prev = A_prev
        self.Z = np.dot(self.W, A_prev) + self.b
        return self.Z
        
    def backward(self, dZ):
        m = self.A_prev.shape[1]
        self.dW = np.dot(dZ, self.A_prev.T) / m
        self.db = np.sum(dZ, axis=1, keepdims=True) / m
        dA_prev = np.dot(self.W.T, dZ)
        return dA_prev
```
### Numerical Stability & Optimizations
> Numerical instability is the silent killer of custom ML engines. Unprotected exponential functions in Softmax result in immediate NaN overflows.
To guarantee stability during Softmax cross-entropy computation, we subtract $\max(Z)$ from the logits before exponentiation:
$$\text{Softmax}(Z_i) = \frac{e^{Z_i - \max(Z)}}{\sum_j e^{Z_j - \max(Z)}}$$

### Experimental Results on MNIST
The custom NumPy engine was evaluated on the MNIST dataset using a 784 -> 128 -> 64 -> 10 architecture with He initialization, Adam optimization, and ReLU activations:

- **Epoch 1**: Test Loss: 0.382 | Test Accuracy: 89.4%
- **Epoch 10**: Test Loss: 0.114 | Test Accuracy: 96.6%
- **Epoch 20**: Test Loss: 0.089 | Test Accuracy: 97.4%

The key takeaway was not merely hitting 97%+ accuracy, but being able to debug gradient flow at any individual weight node.

title: Why I Rebuilt My Portfolio with Zero Dependencies and Pure ES Modules
subtitle: Eliminating build steps, npm bloat, and bundler overhead in favor of pure HTML5, Vanilla CSS, and native ES6 modules.
excerpt: Modern web development is bloated with build tools. Here is why building with native ES modules and zero npm packages yields superior speed and clarity.
content: Modern web development often defaults to heavy bundlers, Webpack configs, Next.js frameworks, and thousands of `node_modules` packages. For a personal developer portfolio, this introduces massive complexity, slow build times, and dependency fragility.
### The Philosophy of Zero-Dependency Web Architecture

When building software from first principles, every layer between your source code and the browser should be justified. Browsers now natively support JavaScript ES6+ Modules (`type="module"`), CSS Custom Properties, and hardware-accelerated rendering.
> Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability. — Edsger W. Dijkstra
### Modular Native ES Modules
Instead of bundling all JavaScript into a monolithic 1MB file, each section of the site is isolated into a native ES module:
### Canvas Math & Physics-Smoothed LERP Animations
To create a dynamic background without external animation libraries like Three.js, the canvas engine utilizes mathematical smoothstep and LERP (Linear Interpolation) dampening:
$$\text{smoothstep}(min, max, x) = 3x^2 - 2x^3$$
$$\text{smoothCollapse}_{t+1} = \text{smoothCollapse}_t + (\text{target} - \text{smoothCollapse}_t) \cdot 0.04$$
This guarantees a smooth 60 FPS animation that gracefully responds to scroll momentum.
### Benchmark Comparisons

- **Build Time**: 0.0 seconds (Zero compile step)
- **JavaScript Size**: ~50 KB total across all 13 modules
- **First Contentful Paint**: < 150ms
- **Maintenance Overhead**: 0 vulnerable dependencies to update

Building without frameworks forces you to understand DOM events, memory management, and CSS layout algorithms at the fundamental level.

title: HandMobile: Real-Time IMU Telemetry & Gesture Controlled Robotics
subtitle: Designing a micro-controller vehicle controlled via IMU wireless telemetry at age 14.
excerpt: Integrating hardware sensors with wireless microcontrollers to map hand gestures directly to motor PWM output in real time.
content: In 2022, I designed and assembled HandMobile — a gesture-controlled robotic vehicle operated via IMU accelerometer telemetry transmitted over RF wireless channels.
### Hardware & Sensor Fusion

The transmitter glove uses an MPU-6050 6-axis gyroscope and accelerometer. Raw accelerometer values suffer from high-frequency motor vibration, while gyroscope values drift over time. To solve this, a complementary filter was implemented on the Arduino:
$$\theta = 0.98 \cdot (\theta + \omega \cdot dt) + 0.02 \cdot a_{\text{raw}}$$
This simple formula fuses the low-pass filtered accelerometer data with the high-pass filtered gyroscope data in real time.
